principle: Proof over confidence. A task is not complete because an agent says it worked. It is complete only when the system holds evidence, from the same execution cycle, that demonstrates the expected behavior.

rules: implemented is not complete. There is no transition from in_progress or implemented directly to complete.
complete is reachable only from verified.
A material change to a verified capability's sources returns it to verification_stale, whatever it was before - including complete.
verification_failed returns to in_progress. It is never re-labelled as verified without a new passing run.

levels.label: Unverified
levels.means: Agent inference or an implementation claim only. No evidence.

levels.label: Static
levels.means: Code review, schema validation, compilation. Proves it parses, not that it works.

levels.label: Deterministic
levels.means: Unit, acceptance, known-answer or regression test passed.

levels.label: Integrated
levels.means: A real command ran against the real local system and succeeded.

levels.label: End to end
levels.means: A real external system was reached and the outcome was re-read or observed.

levels.label: Operational
levels.means: The behavior has succeeded under actual scheduled or production use.

level_note: Not everything needs level 5. A fuel calculator is entirely trustworthy at level 2. A Sheets write needs level 4 before anyone may call it working. A morning briefing needs an observed scheduled run before level 5.

claim_to_minimum_proof.proof: Actual CLI execution with exit code and captured output.
Real external request and validated response.
Browser interaction with a DOM assertion.
Pre-state capture, mutation, post-state re-read, before/after comparison.

proof_matching_rules: A passing unit test proves the function behaves correctly for the inputs tested. It does not prove an integration works.
A mocked response proves the parser handles a fixture. It does not prove the live provider is reachable with our credentials.
A successful site build proves the site compiles. It does not prove the Command Center's acceptance behavior - which is why cc:test runs in CI.
Evidence below a capability's required level leaves it NOT VERIFIED, however much of that evidence exists.
invalidation_rule: Verification records a fingerprint of the sources it covered. When those sources change, the verification goes stale and must be re-run. Proof from last Tuesday says nothing about code changed today.
reporting_rule: Report proof, not adjectives. Never 'sync is working' - always the claim, the level, the evidence and the timestamp. 'I believe X but cannot prove X from a sufficiently fresh source' is a valid and useful answer.
recommendation_support_rule: A recommendation's confidence derives from the evidence state of its material inputs, never from the model's own certainty. Report coverage as verified inputs over material inputs, and always name what is unresolved.

input_evidence_classes.verified: Externally verified fact or a passing verification.
input_evidence_classes.modeled: A computed result whose calculator is verified.
input_evidence_classes.planning_assumption: A placeholder the model plans on.
input_evidence_classes.unresolved: No canonical value: missing evidence or conflicting sources.
